claims.text: Docker keeps a container's output with that container (one log file per container); docker compose logs reads only the service's existing containers, so after a recreate (docker compose up -d with a new image) or docker compose down, the old container's output is out of reach.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: json-file driver (one file per container); compose networking (old container removed on up); guides/golang (container metadata removed); docker compose logs

claims.text: In Đơn Hàng @stage-2, Alloy (config.alloy) finds the containers of Compose project donhang through the Docker socket (discovery.docker, filter label com.docker.compose.project=donhang, refresh_interval 5s), reads their output (loki.source.docker) and sends every line to Loki (loki.write).

discovery.relabel rule with source_labels [__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_service] and target_label service (default action replace) gives each stream the label service=<Compose service>, e.g. service="api".
claims.source_hint: Grafana Alloy docs: discovery.docker (exported __meta_docker_container_label_<name>), discovery.relabel (rule, default action replace)

claims.text: loki.source.docker reads the logs of the given Docker targets through the Docker daemon (host unix:///var/run/docker.sock), applies relabel_rules, and forwards entries to loki.write, which pushes them to http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push.

docker-compose.yml@stage-2: alloy mounts /var/run/docker.sock read-only; loki (grafana/loki:3.5.12) publishes no port and stores data in the named volume loki-data at /loki; both carry profiles: [monitoring].
Because Loki keeps received lines in its own storage (volume loki-data), lines from a removed or recreated container remain queryable in Loki.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: Loki architecture/storage (filesystem); examples/don-hang @ stage-2 loki.yml

claims.text: A log stream is the set of log lines sharing the same set of labels; each distinct combination of label values is a separate stream.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: Labels (Understand labels), Loki overview

claims.text: Loki indexes only the labels (metadata) of log streams, not the content of log lines; the lines are stored grouped by stream.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: Loki overview / Get started (index only metadata)

claims.text: A LogQL log query is a stream selector ({service="api"}) answered from the index, optionally followed by a pipeline of stages after |, which process the lines of the selected streams (filter, parse).
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: LogQL > Log queries (log stream selector, log pipeline)

claims.text: The | json parser extracts all JSON properties of each line as labels for that query; nested properties are flattened with _ as separator (State.StatusCode -> State_StatusCode).
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: LogQL > Log queries > Parser expression > JSON

claims.text: A label filter expression such as State_StatusCode >= 500 compares the extracted value as a number and keeps only matching lines; State_Path = "/api/v1/orders/42" is a string equality label filter.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: LogQL > Log queries > Label filter expression

claims.text: datasources.yml@stage-2:14-20: second data source name Loki, uid loki, type loki, access proxy, url http://loki:3100; Loki has no page of its own in the lab, it is queried from Grafana.

loki-query.sh@stage-2 runs inside the lab box (on the donhang network, via lab-run.sh), places an order for productId 999 (FK -> 500), then queries Loki's query_range API at http://loki:3100 with the LogQL query, retrying up to 30x; last line prints fields with jq.

Filtering by text or by a parsed field reads through the lines of the selected streams in the time range, so a narrow selector and short range reduce the work; {service="api"} | json | State_StatusCode >= 500 over a week is slower than over an hour.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: Query best practices (narrow label selectors, time range)

claims.text: Putting an unbounded value such as an order id in a label creates one stream per value (high cardinality), which grows Loki's index and degrades Loki's performance; keep labels to few values and filter lines instead.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Loki docs: Cardinality; Label best practices

claims.text: Grafana Explore (/explore) lets you pick a data source (Loki) and run a LogQL query; the Loki query editor has Builder and Code modes.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Explore; Loki data source > Query editor (Builder/Code mode)

claims.text: In the running lab, Loki has label service with values incl. api and db; {service="db"} returns PostgreSQL's plain-text lines (e.g. 'LOG:  database system is ready to accept connections') — checked via Loki HTTP API 2026-09-30.
/var/run/docker.sock is the Docker daemon's Unix socket, the file through which a program (client) talks to Docker; docker-compose.yml@stage-2 mounts it read-only into the alloy container.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: engine/manage-resources/contexts (unix:///var/run/docker.sock); examples/don-hang @ stage-2 docker-compose.yml:302
